title: "Design Lab: Nearby Friends with Expiring Location State"
---

# Design Lab: Nearby Friends with Expiring Location State

Extend the [proximity service](08-proximity-service.qmd) from static places to consenting friends with moving locations. The main new constraints are update ordering, expiry, and authorization. A point in an index is not permission to reveal it.

## Contract and data model

Use authenticated `PUT /me/location` and `GET /me/nearby-friends`. Store account ID, device/session epoch, sequence, coordinates, server receipt time, and expiry. Define which device is authoritative if an account has several devices. For the first lab allow one active sharing session, issued by the server.

Reject updates whose `(session_epoch, sequence)` is older than the stored value. Allocate epochs monotonically and invalidate old sessions when a new one begins. Use server receipt time for TTL; a client's wall clock must not keep a location alive indefinitely.

Represent the update boundary in Go as a conditional store operation:

```go
type LocationUpdate struct {
	UserID          string
	Epoch, Sequence uint64
	Lat, Lon        float64
}

type LocationStore interface {
	ApplyIfNewer(context.Context, LocationUpdate) (bool, error)
}
```

This interface sketch needs an atomic compare-and-update implementation. A Go mutex protects one process; multiple servers need database conditional updates or an equivalent shared-store primitive.

## Query path and visibility

Find nearby candidates using the spatial index, join current friendship and sharing state, discard expired entries, and return only authorized results. Recheck authorization close to response construction, with a defined policy for concurrent revocation. Do not return precise coordinates if the product only needs distance bands.

TTL cleanup improves storage use, but reads must enforce expiry even if the cleanup worker is late. Keep tombstones or version fences long enough that delayed updates cannot recreate a revoked location. Partitioning by geography requires coordinated movement between old and new cells; a simpler first design keeps the location row authoritative and treats cell membership as a rebuildable index.

If clients subscribe over WebSockets, coalesce movement updates and use bounded per-client queues. Disconnect a slow subscriber rather than buffering every location forever. After reconnect, send an authorized current snapshot and resume from a defined event position.

## Failure evidence

Deliver sequence 8 before sequence 7 and assert the stored position remains 8. Expire a location with a fake clock, revoke consent during a pending update, and replay an old-session message after a new session starts. No query may reveal expired or revoked locations according to the stated policy.

Move repeatedly across a cell boundary and verify no stale index entry becomes authoritative. Measure update-to-query lag, discarded stale updates, expired-entry filtering, and outbound queue size. Use synthetic users and locations for repeatable fixtures.
